meta.note: Region/time-period priors given to the AI as CONTEXT ONLY: a mild hint, never proof, never a filter. The owner's provenance always wins. Built from the published sources below; wording is ours.

sources.name: Hill Country Archeological Association, Dart and Arrow Point Typology (after Turner, Hester & McReynolds 2011)
Texas State University, Exploring Spring Lake: Central Texas chronology

packs.label: Central Texas (Edwards Plateau / Blackland Prairie margin)

periods_bp.Paleoindian: about 13,500 to 8,800 BP (Clovis, Folsom, Plainview, Golondrina, Angostura)
periods_bp.Middle Archaic: about 5,750 to 4,200 BP (Early Triangular, Nolan, Travis)
periods_bp.Late Archaic: about 4,200 to 1,270 BP (Bulverde, Pedernales, Castroville, Montell, Marcos, Ensor, Frio, Fairland)
periods_bp.Late Prehistoric: about 1,270 BP to about AD 1550 (arrow points: Scallorn, Edwards, Perdiz)

common_natural_lookalikes: caliche (white chalky calcium carbonate crust or nodule)
coarse sandstone or conglomerate cobbles with quartz pebbles
chert nodules with an intact rind
river-tumbled or plow-damaged chert with random edge chips
packs.note: Most chert in Central Texas is plentiful and many natural pieces are fractured by frost, heat, rivers, plows and machinery, so flaking evidence needs more than one feature.
